description:

Momin Hospital is a trusted healthcare provider based in Kabul, Afghanistan, dedicated to delivering high-quality medical services to the community.
With a team of experienced specialists and professional medical staff, the hospital is committed to providing compassionate care, accurate diagnosis, and advanced treatment solutions.
Our mission is to improve the health and well-being of our patients through modern medical practices, ethical standards, and patient-centered services.

Job Descriptions

The IT Assistant will provide technical support to employees, maintain computer systems and networks, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, and assist in ensuring the smooth operation of all IT equipment and services.

title: Chief Information Technology Officer
description:
Role Summary
The CIO does strategic planning, technology management, resource allocation, and budgeting for Computer Services, including the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, servers, software application development, reporting, interfaces with third-party systems, user training, identification.

Duties and Responsibilities
1. Develop and implement the bank’s technology strategy aligned with business goals.
2. Collaborate with executive leadership to identify opportunities for technology-driven improvements.
3. Oversee the design, implementation, and maintenance of IT infrastructure, ensuring high availability and performance for servers, storage, and cloud services.
4. Direct the management of network architecture, ensuring robust connectivity and security.
5. Implement best practices for network performance monitoring and optimization.
6. Lead the development and deployment of banking applications that enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.
7. Ensure that applications are scalable, secure, and compliant with industry regulations.
8. Establish and enforce IT security policies to safeguard sensitive data and maintain regulatory compliance.
9. Conduct regular security assessments and audits to identify vulnerabilities.
10. Oversee database architecture, ensuring data integrity, availability, and security.
11. Implement data management best practices to support analytics and reporting needs.
12. Build and lead a high-performing IT team through mentoring, coaching, and professional development.
13. Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement within the IT department.
14. Manage relationships with technology vendors and service providers to ensure quality service delivery.
15. Negotiate contracts and agreements to optimize costs and service levels.
16. Develop and manage the IT budget, ensuring effective allocation of resources and monitor expenditures and implement cost-control measures where necessary.

Job Requirements
Educational Qualifications:
• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; Master’s degree in computer will be preferred.
• Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCNA or PMP may be preferred.
Relevant Experience:
• Proven experience in a senior IT leadership role, preferably within the banking or financial services sector for more than 4 years.
• Baking Experience.
• Digitalization Experience.
• Familiarity with Islamic Banking and Products.
SKILLS & COMPETENCIES:
• Strong technical knowledge in infrastructure/system administration, networking, application development, IT security, and database management.
• Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects and lead cross-functional teams.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
• Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive approach to technology challenges.
• Knowledge of regulatory requirements relevant to banking technology.

title: Pediatrician
description:
About Bakhter Development Network - BDN
Bakhter Development Network (BDN) was established and registered in 2001 with the Ministry of Economics in Afghanistan as an Afghan, non-political, non-profit, and non-governmental organization. BDN operates in line with its constitution in three sectors: education, health, and agriculture and livestock. With its current focus on public health and nutrition services, BDN's mission is to assist communities in the achievement of their own development goals, while its vision is a world of enabled communities working toward a brighter future.
Currently, BDN is involved in implementing different health projects across multiple provinces of Afghanistan, such as BPHS-EPHS projects in Balkh and vertical projects like CBNI, TSFP, PHNS, FSAC, GC7, S-WIFS, and RMNCAH/SRH and PSS services in provinces such as Balkh, Badakhshan, Baghlan, Faryab, Sar-e-Pol, Jawzjan, Samangan, Takhar, Kapisa, Ghazni, Kunduz, Paktia, Paktika, Khost, Kabul, Parwan, Panjshir, and Maidan Wardak.
BDN, in more than 20 years of its operation, has made impressive contributions in promoting access to quality healthcare and has developed a reputable track record in the effective implementation of numerous projects within the country. BDN adheres to the policy of equal employment opportunities, and its hiring process is based on evaluation by knowledge, skill, work experience, and ability, without regard to age, sex, race, religion, ethnicity, or physical status.

Job Descriptions
Objective:
The pediatric specialist is responsible for identifying and treating emergency patients, particularly those with urgent and complex cases. They are also responsible for diagnosing diseases and recommending medications at the hospital.
Key Responsibilities:
Conducted examinations; diagnosed; and treated pediatric patients, including those with infectious diseases, in accordance with the standards set by the Ministry of Public Health, including comprehensive childhood illness treatments.
Identify and report issues that interfere with healthcare services.
Identify and hospitalize emergency and complicated pediatric cases.
Complete patient files by taking medical histories, conducting physical examinations, and prescribing treatments according to disease diagnosis based on standard guidelines.
Monitor hospitalized patients during their stay based on progress notes.
Hospitalize patients with moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and diagnose and treat malnutrition-related diseases.
Participate in training sessions provided by the implementing organization.
Attend hospital monthly meetings and committees as required.
Refer patients to other well-equipped centers for further examination and treatment based on diagnosis.
Maintain the registration book, referral forms, and discharge letters, and ensure continuous documentation of patient diagnoses, medication recommendations, and referrals to higher centers, along with other necessary advice during examinations.
Collaborate with all departments of the health center, including providing practical training.
Perform specialized procedures for patients in need and train junior doctors in these procedures.
Possess sufficient knowledge of Afghanistan’s Basic Package of Health Services (BPHS) and implement it in practice.
Adhere to night duty shifts based on the monthly duty roster.
Carry out additional tasks assigned by the relevant supervisor or organization officials.

Job Requirements
A specialty degree in pediatrics from a recognized entity is required.
At least 5 years of experience in the field.
Prior experience in a similar role is an advantage.
Strong communication skills.
Proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing Dari, Pashto, and English.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel is essential.
Demonstrated organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively under pressure and take initiative.
Integrity and a strong commitment to organizational goals are essential.

Make sure the Data Center standard procedure followed by the team, units and vendor
efficiently.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience in Solaris, Linux, Unix, and Windows system administration within enterprise or data center environments.
Strong knowledge of Active Directory, PowerShell scripting, virtualization, storage technologies, server hardware, operating systems, networking, security, and disaster recovery.
Excellent communication, documentation, reporting, and problem-solving skills.

The ACMEG has been serving the Carpet industry for a long time, with a history dating back 58 years. In 1346, Carpet industry traders established the union to promote coherence in their activities. Eventually, it transformed into the Afghanistan Carpet Manufacturers & Exporters Guild and established representative offices in different zones to defend the Carpet sector. This organization is defined as an independent, non-governmental, non-political, and non-profit institution.
Currently, the ACMEG has three representative offices in Mazar-e-Sharif, Herat, and Nangarhar. It plays a crucial role in institutionalizing the process of reforms and export progress in the country. The ACMEG acts as a bridge between Carpet industry leaders, traders, investors, donors, media, and the government to help them achieve their goals. It collaborates with the government in policy formulation processes and provides necessary consultations to ensure the increase of national revenues, preservation of carpet sector interests, and purchasing power of the people.
In order to develop trade and investment, the ACMEG has undertaken programs to enhance the domestic carpet production. It believes that creating an appropriate environment for cohesion in the country is one of the primary needs of carpet industry players. Therefore, the ACMEG offers services such as advocacy and representation of the carpet sector, establishment of international relations, and collaboration with the government. The executive board provides necessary services to the carpet sector.

About Afghanistan Social and Legal Organization (ASLO)
Afghanistan Social and Legal Organization (ASLO) – Organizational Profile
Registration and Legal Status
Afghanistan Social and Legal Organization (ASLO) is an Afghan non-governmental, non-political, non-profit, and non-partisan organization with full legal entity status in Afghanistan. The organization was informally established in 2012 and officially registered with the Ministry of Economy of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan in 2013 under Registration Number (2852) through the NGOs Department of the Ministry of Economy in Kabul, Afghanistan.
Since its establishment, ASLO has remained committed to supporting vulnerable and underserved communities across Afghanistan through humanitarian assistance, sustainable development initiatives, education, healthcare, livelihoods support, legal aid, and community empowerment programs.
ASLO Vision
ASLO envisions a peaceful, developed, and prosperous Afghanistan where every individual has access to quality education, healthcare, justice, sustainable livelihoods, and equal opportunities, and where women, children, and vulnerable populations fully enjoy their rights, dignity, protection, and social inclusion.
ASLO Mission
ASLO works to empower individuals, families, communities, women, youth, and institutions through humanitarian assistance, education, rights advocacy, research, capacity building, access to justice, peacebuilding, livelihood support, and sustainable development interventions aimed at improving resilience and promoting long-term social and economic development.
Core Areas of Intervention
ASLO currently implements humanitarian and development programs across multiple sectors in Afghanistan, including:
Humanitarian Assistance and Emergency Response
Education and Education in Emergencies (EiE)
Health and Nutrition
Legal Aid and Access to Justice
Women Empowerment and Gender Equality
Child Protection and Social Protection
Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)
Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR)
Food Security and Livelihoods
Agriculture and Livestock
Rural Development and Community Resilience
Refugee, IDP, and Returnee Support
Research, Assessments, Surveys, Monitoring, and Evaluations
Community Capacity Building and Peace Promotion
Construction and Infrastructure Support
In addition, ASLO integrates key cross-cutting priorities throughout all interventions, including gender mainstreaming, protection, child safeguarding, disability inclusion, environmental protection and climate resilience, accountability to affected populations, research and evidence-based programming, and infrastructure development.

Job Descriptions
Purpose of the Position
The Internal Audit Officer will provide independent, objective assurance and advisory services designed to strengthen ASLO’s governance, risk management, accountability and internal control systems. The post holder will conduct risk-based reviews of financial, operational, programme, procurement, human resources, logistics, safeguarding and compliance processes; identify control gaps; recommend practical corrective actions; and follow up management implementation.
The position must remain independent from day-to-day operational and financial decision-making. The Internal Audit Officer will have authorized access to relevant records, systems, premises and personnel, subject to ASLO’s confidentiality, data-protection and safeguarding requirements.
Reporting, Independence and Authority
• Report functionally to the Board of Trustees or its designated Audit Committee and administratively to the General Director.
• Communicate significant or urgent risks directly and confidentially through the approved functional reporting line.
• Maintain independence, objectivity and professional scepticism and disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest before accepting an assignment.
• Avoid auditing activities for which the post holder recently held direct operational responsibility.
• Obtain unrestricted, timely access to records, staff, assets, systems and project locations required for approved audit work.
• Protect confidential information and use audit evidence only for authorized organizational purposes.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Risk-Based Audit Planning
• Develop and regularly update ASLO’s audit universe and organization-wide risk assessment.
• Prepare a risk-based annual internal audit plan, resource estimate and audit schedule for approval by the Board/Audit Committee.
• Define clear objectives, scope, criteria, methodology and work programmes for each audit engagement.
• Adjust the audit plan when material changes in funding, programmes, operations, systems or risk exposure occur.
• Coordinate audit timing with management while preserving the independence and scope of the internal audit function.
Financial, Grant and Donor Compliance
• Review accounting records, bank and cash controls, reconciliations, advances, payroll, taxes, supporting documents, budget controls and financial reporting.
• Assess the accuracy, completeness, authorization, eligibility, allowability and allocability of project expenditures.
